summary: Anyone, man or woman, who swaps a plain animal for a korban animal makes both animals holy, even though swapping is not allowed. Kohanim may swap only their own korbanos, and Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri argue about a bechor a Kohen was given.

chunks.en: Everyone can make a swap,
chunks.explain: A swap puts a plain animal in place of a korban animal.
chunks.st: Everyone substitutes a non-sacred animal for a consecrated animal,

words.note: To swap (temurah) is to say a plain animal is in place of a korban animal; then both are holy.

chunks.en: both men and women.
chunks.st: both men and women.

chunks.en: but that if he did swap,

chunks.en: the swap works, and he gets the punishment of forty lashes.
chunks.st: the substitution takes effect, and the non-sacred animal becomes consecrated, and the consecrated animal remains sacred. And the one who substituted the non-sacred animal incurs the forty [sofeg et ha’arba’im] lashes.

words.note: The punishment of lashes (malkus) given by a beis din.

It is written: “He shall neither exchange it, nor substitute it, good for bad, or bad for good; and if he substitutes an animal for an animal, then both it and its substitute shall be sacred” (Leviticus 27:10). The mishna enumerates the consecrated and non-sacred animals this verse applies to.

summary: You can swap any kind of animal for a korban: cattle for sheep, sheep for goats, males for females, and blemished for unblemished. The Rabbis say you may even swap one animal for many, but Rabbi Shimon says only one for one.

chunks.en: and sheep for cattle,

summary: You cannot swap a body part of an animal for an unborn calf, or swap parts for a whole animal. Rabbi Yosei says that if you swap a leg of an animal for a korban, the whole animal becomes the swap.

chunks.en: We cannot swap body parts for unborn babies,
chunks.st: One does not substitute non-sacred limbs for consecrated fetuses, i.e., if one says that a certain limb of a non-sacred animal is substituted for a fetus in the womb of a consecrated animal, it is not consecrated.

words.note: A baby animal still inside its mother.

summary: Some things spread their status only as much as they really are inside a mixture: terumah mixed into other food, sour dough made with terumah, and drawn water poured into a mikveh.
stIntro: If teruma, the portion of the produce designated for the priest, was intermingled with non-sacred produce, and it is impossible to distinguish between them, if the ratio of non-sacred produce to teruma was less than one hundred to one, the teruma is not nullified and all the produce is forbidden to those for whom teruma is forbidden.

chunks.he: אֵין הַמְדֻמָּע מְדַּמֵּעַ אֶלָּא לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן.
chunks.en: A mixture with terumah in it makes more food into a terumah mixture only by counting how much terumah is really there.
chunks.explain: Terumah is food for Kohanim only.
chunks.st: If the mixture was then intermingled with other non-sacred produce, that mixture renders it a mixture of teruma only according to the calculation of the percentage of the original teruma produce in the entire mixture.

chunks.he: אֵין הַמְחֻמָּץ מְחַמֵּץ אֶלָּא לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן.
chunks.en: Dough made sour with terumah makes other dough sour only by counting.
chunks.st: And dough that was leavened with a teruma leavening agent is forbidden to those for whom teruma is forbidden even if the ratio between the non-sacred and the teruma is greater than one hundred to one. If a portion of that dough was intermingled with non-sacred dough, it leavens only according to the calculation of the percentage of the original leavening agent in the entire dough, and the second dough is forbidden only if the quantity of the original teruma leavening agent inside it is sufficient to leaven it.

chunks.st: And if three log of drawn water were poured into a ritual bath with less than forty se’a to complete the requisite forty se’a, the ritual bath is invalidated. But drawn water invalidates

summary: Water for the red heifer becomes special only when the ashes are put into the water. Also, a swapped animal cannot make another swap, and the Rabbis say a baby of a korban cannot make a swap either.

chunks.en: Water does not become water for purifying

chunks.st: becomes water of purification only with the placement of the ashes into the water, but not by placement of water onto the ashes.

chunks.en: A beis haperas does not make another beis haperas,
chunks.st: And one beit haperas does not create another beit haperas.
chunks.stMore: The Sages decreed ritual impurity on a field in which a grave was plowed, scattering the bones throughout the field. This field is called a beit haperas. That impurity extends to the area of one hundred cubits surrounding the grave. Nevertheless, they did not decree impurity on the second field if one plowed from that field into another field.

words.note: A field where a grave was plowed up, so bones may be spread around.

chunks.en: and there is no terumah after terumah,
chunks.st: And there is no teruma after teruma.
chunks.stMore: Once one designates produce from his crop as teruma, if he then designates additional produce from that crop as teruma, it is not teruma.

chunks.en: and a swap does not make another swap,
chunks.st: And a substitute animal that was consecrated when it was substituted for a consecrated animal does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute; rather, it remains non-sacred.

chunks.en: and the baby of a korban does not make a swap.
chunks.st: And the offspring born of a consecrated animal that was not consecrated itself does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute.

summary: Birds and flour offerings cannot make a swap, and neither can korbanos of the whole community, of partners, or things given for fixing the Beis HaMikdash. Rabbi Shimon learns this from the animal maaser.

chunks.en: Bird and flour korbanos cannot make a swap,
chunks.st: The birds sacrificed as offerings, i.e., doves and pigeons, and the meal offerings do not render non-sacred items exchanged for them substitutes,

words.note: A mincha is a korban made of flour.

chunks.en: because the Torah speaks only about an animal.
chunks.st: as only the term “an animal” is stated with regard to substitution, in the verse: “And if he substitutes an animal for an animal” (Leviticus 27:10).

chunks.en: The community and partners cannot make a swap,
chunks.st: A consecrated animal belonging to the community or to partners does not render a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute,

chunks.en: Things given for fixing the Beis HaMikdash cannot make a swap.
chunks.st: Items consecrated for Temple maintenance do not render non-sacred items exchanged for them substitutes.

chunks.en: Wasn't maaser already included with all korbanos?
chunks.st: The animal tithe was included in the category of all offerings,

words.note: Every tenth animal born, given as a korban.

chunks.en: Then why was it named by itself?

He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad, neither shall he substitute for it; and if he substitutes it, then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be sacred” (Leviticus 27:32–33)? Rabbi Shimon explains: It was singled out to juxtapose substitution to the animal tithe,

chunks.en: To teach from it:
chunks.st: to tell you:

chunks.en: Just as maaser is a korban of one person,
chunks.st: Just as the animal tithe is brought exclusively as an individual offering, so too, all offerings that render their substitutes sacred are individual offerings,

chunks.en: korbanos of the community are left out.
chunks.st: excluding communal offerings and the offerings of partners from the halakha of substitution.

chunks.en: Just as maaser is a korban for the mizbe'ach,
chunks.st: And just as the animal tithe is an offering sacrificed on the altar, so too, all offerings that render their substitutes sacred are offerings sacrificed on the altar,

chunks.en: things for fixing the Beis HaMikdash are left out.
chunks.st: excluding items consecrated for Temple maintenance from the halakha of substitution.
